chapter.title: The Case of the Upward Center Fill

items.alt: A side view of the room: a center-fill loudspeaker tilted up at the ceiling. Its sound reaches seat 13 twice — directly, and late after bouncing off the ceiling.
narration: The complaint always comes from the same ten seats — dead center.

items.alt: A graph of the sound at seat 13 swings between sharp peaks and deep nulls — comb filtering. Ray explains.

bubbles.text: Direct sound gets there first. The ceiling bounce arrives a few milliseconds late — and they fight. That's comb filtering.

items.alt: The fill loudspeaker is re-aimed flat at the listeners; a green check mark. Maya points at the seats.

bubbles.text: Aim at people, not the ceiling. Every time.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A few milliseconds between a direct and a reflected sound can hollow out clarity. In audio, geometry is part of the mix.
